scenarios.title: two-machine send, reply, and ack
assertions: Docker automation uses real current-source Linux Tailcat sidecars and an owned relay on an internal bridge
DERP and STUN use only the relay IPv4 verified against its running owned container, internal bridge network ID and private IPAM subnet
managed join failures retain bounded public code/error and per-step diagnostics without invite links, bearers or private address credentials
private Unix backends dial reported sidecar slots without direct TCP Zenoh links
fresh task-owned device keys and normal org invite/join establish membership before traffic
each container initializes an independent persistent OS machine-id before device provisioning; restart preserves it without disabling copied-home identity protection
canonical target discovery
durable acceptance receipt
correlated replyTo
ack-only removes pending delivery
no automatic reply loop
private backend and sidecar slot mappings recover after container restart from launcher environment and durable node state
offline queueing delivers after recipient restart
daemon restart self-heals the mesh
advertised official agent a.<id> targetUri delivers verbatim
restart-window message delivers after self-heal
suspend/resume (docker pause) delivers exactly once
mesh partition heal (network disconnect/connect) delivers exactly once
a delivered message's terminal state is a durable fetched record the sender pulls after the fact
the verdict survives the sender's own restart and later phases
a container that never held the message pulls the same fetched verdict across namespaces
an undeliverable message reads pending with a hold deadline, then expired on its holder's TTL with no operator command
the expired verdict is pulled from a container holding no record of the message
a cross-host status pull collects every holder that answered, not one reply consolidated by key
the recipient's own record wins the merge over a sender's receipt mirror, independent of clock order
a status verdict reports the holder set and every known reply loss it was merged from

mailbox transfer starts only after public host online and all canonical peer-agent targets disappear and the owned recipient container is confirmed exited within the original shared 90s; a retained unknown host row is not an offline verdict
with a mailbox present an undeliverable message is taken by the mailbox and the sender holds nothing
a mailbox that is neither sender nor recipient records expired on its own TTL
the sender pulls the mailbox's expired verdict across containers with holder naming the mailbox
a mailbox delivers held custody when the recipient returns and appears in the sender's holder set
every exit removes owned daemon and relay containers, private network and labeled volumes
